header: Branch adaptive-instruments. Main control: contour_parallel (the operator roughs mostly with it; AgentSearch is a secondary column, at the right). contour_parallel columns are at f32401326, from the new copies corne_job_corrected_c12_contour_parallel.toml (byte-identical to the original corne_job_corrected.toml) and wanaka200_mt1_c12_rough_only_contour_parallel.toml (the rough-only copy with '2 Back Rough' back to contour_parallel). Corne geodesic columns zigzag, zigzag_v2 and one-way are at 13667775d (binary 18:23:12); zigzag_pick is at f32401326; all run once with --sim-artifact in the fixture worktree; the binary in the line below is the f32401326 build. The Corne AgentSearch control is the D-FIX1 run at cdc9814e (byte parity: AgentSearch output is the same at every later commit), with its --sim-artifact rerun at 31935b89 (byte-equal program.nc). wanaka200 columns: AgentSearch and zigzag at 31935b89, zigzag_v2 at 4cceca914. The 31935b89 --sim-artifact reruns used a rebuild from the same source; each rerun's program.nc is byte-equal to its page run. Rough ops only. No ranking.
method: Load rule (D-FIX6, from C30): the load shares and the producer split count every cutting sample whose intent is a cut (clearing_cut), of any kinematics, so the draped helix-kinematics samples of the perimeter sweep and the waterline are now in; entry (plunge, helix, ramp) and link samples stay out. Correction (D16c): the earlier version of this page counted only straight (linear) cutting samples in the load share and left out the fitted arcs, so its shares for zigzag_v2 (4.53%) and one-way (4.39%) on Corne were too high; every share below now counts linear and arc samples. Corne geodesic columns are at 13667775d (C26b: held links that cross terrain fall back to the lifted path, which removes the C26 export refusal; C28: the per-piece zigzag pick); the earlier Corne columns (31935b89, 4cceca914, 6ce373922) are in P15_D_verify.md. The zigzag_pick column is at f32401326 (C29: the pick scores the plans by their 3D plunges): it keeps plan A (plain zigzag) at all four levels, so its toolpath equals the zigzag column (56 plunges, 2607 s), while generating '3D Rough 1' in 4.33 s against 2.33 s for zigzag. The score covers the region bodies: its 4, 5, 5 and 4 plunges for A equal the body plunges per level (P3_C22_3d_turns.md section 10d). The other plunges of a level are outside the score: the op's first entry, the waterline cleanup (2, 2, 2 and 31 per section 10d) and the regions that the F-038 forecast skips. Two counts of the level plunges: 7, 7, 7 and 35 (the trace's plunge-entry items, placed by move order, each level running from its first cut move to the next level's) and 10, 6, 6 and 34 (this page's red rings, placed by the Z of the move after the entry's last rapid). The first entry after each region body is not scored (G-PICKEXIT in DEFECTS.md). At 13667775d the 2D-scored pick (C28) kept plan B at every level and plunged more (67). Source of the link tags: the per-move intent of the closing simulation of each run (simulation.json, the source_intent of the move's first sample; a move with no sample keeps the trace span tag). A keep-down link count is a run of consecutive link moves. Entry rings and depth levels come from the semantic_trace of each run's tp_*.json ('plunge entry' spans, 'Global Z' labels), matched to the exported G-code by move index (move i = command line i+1 of the op's section). G2/G3 arcs are drawn and measured as chords. Turns carry no tag in the trace, so they are drawn blue with the cuts. Corne: images show '3D Rough 1' only; the table gives both rough ops. Corne exports used --accept-unmodeled-tool-load (the skipped 'Waterline 3' has a stale sim). wanaka200 runs use wanaka200_mt1_c12_rough_only.toml: the c12 copy with 7 non-rough ops removed (1 Pin Drill, 3 Holes, 4 Rivers, 5 Lakes, 7 tier-A R2.0, 7b tier-B rest R1.0, 8 Pencil R0.5) so the 0.1 mm rest rule does not apply; the earlier c12 copy also carries the Drill depth to floor migration (R-B/F19). wanaka200 sim cell 1.0 mm (coarsened for time).
turn_note: Planned zigzag turns that are not cut (heavy C12 test: 95 planned, 56 cut): in the one-level C12 test (46 planned, 27 cut) a temporary probe found that each of the 19 is a plunge. The cleaned plan lifts the cutter at the end of the arc and re-enters at the turn's start, so the turn runs as the first step out of that plunge (most of them at the island side); the heavy test's 39 were not probed one by one.
